SCRIPTURES.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good.
The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.
Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the LORD.
The LORD bless thee, and keep thee:
And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.
Man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live.
Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.
Whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God:
For man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.
The battle is the LORD'S, and he will give you into our hands.
The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer;
How long halt ye between two opinions? if the LORD be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him.
Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.
Seek the LORD and his strength, seek his face continually.
If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face... then will I hear from heaven.
For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.
The joy of the LORD is your strength.
And who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth:
The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.
The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?
God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help. My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth.
Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.
Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it:
For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder.
But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles.
But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him.
For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways.
The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?
For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil.
Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not.
It is of the LORD'S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you.
The soul that sinneth, it shall die.
Our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace.
My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me.
My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.
I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy.
Can two walk together, except they be agreed?
For the day of the LORD is near upon all the heathen.
Salvation is of the LORD.
What doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
The LORD is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.
The just shall live by his faith.
The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy.
Now therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts; Consider your ways.
Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.
Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse... and prove me now herewith, saith the LORD of hosts.
Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:
For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?
If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth.
For with God nothing shall be impossible.
And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise.
For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.
I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:
I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me.
Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.
For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;
And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God.
If thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.
And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.
Know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you?
God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able.
And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.
Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away.
My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.
I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance.
For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God:
Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.
Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men;
Pray without ceasing.
If any would not work, neither should he eat.
Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers.
For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.
All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction.
For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men,
That the communication of thy faith may become effectual by the acknowledging of every good thing which is in you in Christ Jesus.
For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword.
Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.
If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally.
But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins.
He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.
And this is love, that we walk after his commandments.
I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.
Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory.
Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him.
And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying.
I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last.

PARABLES.name: The Sower
PARABLES.theme: Different responses to the word.

PARABLES.name: The Wheat and Tares
PARABLES.theme: Good and evil remain together until judgment.

PARABLES.name: The Mustard Seed
PARABLES.theme: The kingdom grows from a small beginning.

PARABLES.name: The Leaven
PARABLES.theme: The kingdom's influence spreads.

PARABLES.name: The Hidden Treasure
PARABLES.theme: The surpassing value of the kingdom.

PARABLES.name: The Pearl of Great Price
PARABLES.theme: The kingdom is worth giving up everything to obtain.

PARABLES.name: The Unforgiving Servant
PARABLES.theme: Those forgiven should forgive.

PARABLES.name: The Labourers in the Vineyard
PARABLES.theme: God's generosity is not governed by human comparison.

PARABLES.name: The Two Sons
PARABLES.theme: Obedience matters more than profession.

PARABLES.name: The Wicked Husbandmen
PARABLES.theme: Rejection of God's messengers and Son.

PARABLES.name: The Marriage Feast
PARABLES.theme: Invitation, response and readiness for the kingdom.

PARABLES.name: The Ten Virgins
PARABLES.theme: Be watchful and prepared.

PARABLES.name: The Talents
PARABLES.theme: Faithful stewardship of what is entrusted.

PARABLES.name: The Good Samaritan
PARABLES.theme: Neighbour-love crosses social boundaries.

PARABLES.name: The Rich Fool
PARABLES.theme: Earthly wealth cannot secure life before God.

PARABLES.name: The Lost Sheep
PARABLES.theme: Joy over recovering the lost.

PARABLES.name: The Lost Coin
PARABLES.theme: Joy over one sinner who repents.

PARABLES.name: The Prodigal Son
PARABLES.theme: Repentance, restoration and the father's welcome.

PARABLES.name: The Rich Man and Lazarus
PARABLES.theme: A reversal after death and the sufficiency of God's revealed warning.

PARABLES.name: The Pharisee and the Publican
PARABLES.theme: Humility and repentance rather than self-righteousness.

DATA.kids: Cain, Abel, Seth; other sons and daughters
DATA.story: The first man. He lived in Eden with Eve, disobeyed God's command concerning the forbidden tree, and was expelled from the garden.

DATA.kids: Cain, Abel, Seth; other sons and daughters
DATA.story: The first woman and Adam's wife. She was deceived by the serpent and ate the forbidden fruit.
The firstborn son of Adam and Eve. He murdered his brother Abel after becoming angry over their offerings.
A keeper of sheep whose offering was regarded by God; he was murdered by his brother Cain.
Born to Adam and Eve after Abel's death; his line continues toward Noah.
A descendant of Seth who walked with God; Genesis says God took him.
Enoch's son and Noah's grandfather; recorded as living 969 years.
Built the ark at God's command and survived the Flood with his household.

DATA.kids: Ishmael, Isaac, Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, Shuah
DATA.story: Patriarch called by God, recipient of the covenant promises and father of Isaac.
Abraham's wife who gave birth to Isaac in old age according to God's promise.
Sarah's Egyptian servant and mother of Ishmael; she encountered the angel of the LORD in the wilderness.

DATA.kids: Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, Kedemah
DATA.story: Abraham's son through Hagar, promised to become the father of twelve princes.
The promised son of Abraham and Sarah, nearly offered by Abraham, and later husband of Rebekah.
Isaac's wife and mother of the twins Esau and Jacob; she helped Jacob receive Isaac's blessing.
Jacob's twin brother who sold his birthright and became associated with Edom.

DATA.kids: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun, Joseph, Benjamin; Dinah
DATA.story: Son of Isaac, renamed Israel, and father of the family that became the tribes of Israel.
Sold into Egypt by his brothers, later rose to power and preserved his family during famine.
Led Israel out of Egypt, received the Law at Sinai, and guided Israel through the wilderness.
Brother of Moses, spokesman for him, and Israel's first high priest.
Sister of Moses and Aaron, called a prophetess, and led women in song after the crossing of the sea.
Moses' successor who led Israel across the Jordan and into Canaan.
Woman of Jericho who hid Israelite spies and was spared when the city fell.
Prophetess and judge who summoned Barak and helped lead Israel during conflict with Sisera.

DATA.kids: Seventy sons are mentioned; Abimelech is named
DATA.story: Judge called by God to defeat Midian with a greatly reduced army.
Rejected son of Gilead who became a judge and military leader; remembered for his tragic vow.
A man of Zorah whose unnamed wife received an angelic announcement that Samson would be born as a Nazirite.
Judge of extraordinary strength who fought the Philistines, was betrayed by Delilah, and died bringing down their temple.
Widow who returned to Bethlehem with Ruth after losing her husband and sons.
Moabite widow loyal to Naomi who married Boaz and became an ancestor of David.
Kinsman-redeemer who married Ruth and became great-grandfather of David.

DATA.kids: Samuel; other sons and daughters through Hannah
DATA.story: Husband of Hannah and father of Samuel, who regularly went to worship at Shiloh.

DATA.kids: Samuel; later three sons and two daughters
DATA.story: Prayed earnestly for a son and dedicated Samuel to the LORD; later sang a famous prayer of thanksgiving.
Priest at Shiloh who mentored Samuel; his sons acted wickedly and his house came under judgment.
Prophet and judge who anointed Saul and later David as kings.

DATA.kids: Jonathan, Abinadab/Ishvi, Malchi-shua, Ish-bosheth; Merab and Michal
DATA.story: Israel's first king, eventually rejected for disobedience and consumed by jealousy toward David.
Saul's son and David's loyal friend who died in battle with his father.

DATA.kids: Amnon, Chileab/Daniel, Absalom, Adonijah, Shephatiah, Ithream, Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon and others; Tamar
DATA.story: Shepherd who defeated Goliath and became king; established Jerusalem as capital and received a dynastic promise.
Wise wife of Nabal who stopped David from bloodshed and later became David's wife.
Wealthy but harsh man who insulted David and later died after Abigail intervened.
Commander of Saul's army who supported Ish-bosheth before transferring allegiance toward David; Joab killed him.
Son of Saul who ruled much of Israel in opposition to David for a short period.
Jonathan's disabled son whom David treated kindly for Jonathan's sake.
Soldier and husband of Bathsheba whose death David arranged after committing adultery with Bathsheba.
David's powerful military commander, known for both loyalty and ruthless violence.

DATA.kids: A son is not named in his story; he is linked genealogically to Eliam
DATA.story: David's counselor who defected to Absalom; his advice was frustrated by Hushai.
David's friend who infiltrated Absalom's court and undermined Ahithophel's counsel.

DATA.kids: Sons are referenced; Chimham is associated with him
DATA.story: An elderly wealthy supporter who supplied David during Absalom's rebellion.
Son of David who tried to claim the throne before Solomon was established as king.
Son of David renowned for wisdom; built the first Temple but later turned toward foreign gods.

DATA.kids: Several sons are named in 2 Chronicles 11
DATA.story: Solomon's son whose harsh policy contributed to the division of the kingdom.
Prophet who opposed Ahab and Jezebel, confronted the prophets of Baal, and was taken up in a whirlwind.
Successor of Elijah whose ministry included numerous miracles and counsel to kings.
King of Israel married to Jezebel; opposed Elijah and promoted Baal worship.
Queen associated with Baal worship and persecution of God's prophets; later killed during Jehu's revolt.
Aramean commander healed of leprosy after obeying Elisha's instruction to wash in the Jordan.

DATA.kids: Sons/descendants are not clearly recorded in his main story
DATA.story: Elisha's servant who secretly took gifts from Naaman and was punished.
Aramean official who became king and later oppressed Israel.
Military commander anointed king who destroyed Ahab's dynasty and killed Jezebel.

DATA.kids: Ahaziah; other royal children are referenced
DATA.story: Queen who seized Judah's throne and attempted to destroy the royal heirs.
High priest who protected Joash, overthrew Athaliah, and restored covenant worship.
Hidden from Athaliah as a child and crowned king at age seven under Jehoiada's protection.
King of Judah who trusted God during Sennacherib's invasion and enacted religious reforms.
Assyrian king who invaded Judah in Hezekiah's reign; Jerusalem was not captured.
Assyrian official who publicly challenged Hezekiah and mocked Judah's trust in God.
King of Assyria who came against Hoshea; Samaria was besieged and the northern kingdom fell to Assyria.
Prophetess consulted after the Book of the Law was found during Josiah's reign.
King of Judah who led major reforms after the Book of the Law was found.
Jeremiah's scribe who wrote and read the prophet's words from a scroll.
Cushite court official who courageously rescued Jeremiah from a cistern.

DATA.kids: No children clearly named in the Bible as his own
DATA.story: Babylonian king who conquered Jerusalem and features prominently in Daniel.
Jewish exile who served foreign kings, interpreted dreams, and survived the lions' den.
One of Daniel's three companions who survived the fiery furnace after refusing idolatry.
One of Daniel's companions preserved in the fiery furnace.
One of Daniel's companions preserved in the fiery furnace.
Jewish queen of Persia who risked her life to intervene against a plot to destroy her people.
Esther's older relative and guardian who uncovered a plot and opposed Haman.
Priest and scribe who taught the Law after the exile.
Governor who led the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls despite opposition.
A prophetess mentioned briefly among those who tried to intimidate Nehemiah.

DATA.kids: Meshullam, Hananiah; Shelomith is named as a daughter
DATA.story: Davidic descendant and governor involved in rebuilding the Temple after exile.

DATA.kids: Seven sons and three daughters initially; later seven sons and three daughters, with Jemimah, Keziah and Keren-happuch named
DATA.story: Righteous man who endured catastrophic suffering and wrestled with questions of justice and faith.
Priest who received Gabriel's announcement of John's birth and was temporarily unable to speak after doubting.
Wife of Zechariah and relative of Mary who conceived John in old age.
Prophetic forerunner of Jesus who preached repentance and baptized in the Jordan.

DATA.kids: Jesus; Jesus' brothers and sisters are mentioned, with interpretation varying by tradition
DATA.story: Mother of Jesus, chosen to conceive by the Holy Spirit and present at key moments in Jesus' life.

DATA.kids: Jesus was regarded as his son; family relationships are interpreted differently across traditions
DATA.story: Mary's husband and Davidic descendant who protected the family after angelic guidance.
Central figure of the New Testament: teacher, Messiah and Son of God in Christianity, crucified and raised from the dead.
A leading apostle who denied Jesus three times, was restored, and became prominent in the early church.
Peter's brother and one of the first disciples of Jesus.
Brother of John and member of Jesus' inner circle; executed under Herod Agrippa I.
Brother of James and prominent apostle present at several major events in Jesus' ministry.
Tax collector called by Jesus to become one of the Twelve.
Apostle who initially doubted reports of the resurrection before encountering the risen Jesus.
One of the Twelve who betrayed Jesus and later died after Jesus was condemned.
Follower of Jesus who witnessed the crucifixion and became an early witness of the empty tomb and risen Christ.
Sister of Mary and Lazarus who welcomed Jesus and confessed faith in him before Lazarus was raised.
Sister of Martha and Lazarus who listened at Jesus' feet and later anointed him with perfume.
Friend of Jesus and brother of Mary and Martha whom Jesus raised from the dead.
Chief tax collector who climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus and responded with repentance and restitution.
Early church servant and powerful witness who was stoned, becoming the first Christian martyr described in Acts.
Former persecutor who encountered Jesus on the Damascus road and became a major missionary and apostle.
Early Christian leader known for encouragement who supported Paul and later traveled with him.
Younger coworker of Paul, son of Eunice and grandson of Lois.
Christian teacher and coworker of Paul who, with Aquila, instructed Apollos more accurately.
Husband of Priscilla, tentmaker and coworker of Paul.
Eloquent Jewish teacher from Alexandria who was instructed more accurately by Priscilla and Aquila.
Seller of purple cloth at Philippi who became a believer and hosted Paul and his companions.

DATA.kids: Household mentioned; children not individually named
DATA.story: Roman centurion whose household received the Holy Spirit after Peter preached to them.

DATA.book: Matthew; Mark; Luke; John; Acts; 1 Timothy
DATA.story: Roman governor who presided over Jesus' trial and authorized the crucifixion.
Elderly prophetess who worshiped at the Temple and spoke about Jesus when he was presented there.

DATA.kids: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, Tiras

Noah's son whose line is traced toward Abraham.
Noah's son and father of four named sons in the Table of Nations.
Son of Japheth and ancestor of peoples named after the Flood.
Son of Japheth whose descendants are linked with maritime peoples.

DATA.kids: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, Sabteca; Nimrod
DATA.story: Son of Ham and father of Nimrod and several named peoples.
A mighty warrior and hunter associated with early kingdoms including Babel.
Father of Abram, Nahor and Haran; moved from Ur and settled in Haran.
Brother of Abram and father of Lot, Milcah and Iscah.
Abraham's nephew who lived near Sodom and escaped its destruction.
King of Salem and priest of God Most High who blessed Abram.

Father of Rebekah and Laban.
Jacob's uncle and employer who repeatedly bargained with and deceived him.

Jacob's son whose line continues through Perez toward David.

Daughter of Jacob and Leah whose story triggered Simeon and Levi's violent revenge.
Jacob's firstborn who tried to rescue Joseph from his brothers.
Moses' father-in-law and priest of Midian who advised Moses about delegated leadership.

Levite who led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron.

Reubenite who joined Korah's rebellion.
Diviner hired by Balak to curse Israel but compelled to bless them.
King of Moab who hired Balaam against Israel.

Captured Kiriath-sepher, married Acsah, and became a judge.

FACT_ROWS: Which prophet anointed both Saul and David as king?
Which prophet confronted David with a parable about a poor man's only ewe lamb after the affair with Bathsheba?
Which prophet healed the Syrian commander Naaman of leprosy?
Which king of Judah, son of Ahaz, received Isaiah's counsel during Sennacherib's invasion and was given fifteen added years of life?
Which king of Judah began to reign at eight years old and heard the Book of the Law read after it was found during temple repairs?
Isaiah saw the Lord high and lifted up in the year that which king died?
Which king of Judah cut Jeremiah's scroll with a penknife and burned it in the fire?
As a consequence of entering the temple to burn incense, which king of Judah was struck with leprosy?
Which king of Israel was anointed by a young prophet sent by Elisha and then struck down the house of Ahab?
Which woman judged Israel while sitting under a palm tree between Ramah and Bethel?
Which judge reduced his army from 32,000 to 300 men at God's direction?
Which priest survived the massacre at Nob and fled to David?
Which priest directed the coup that crowned the boy king Joash and ended Athaliah's rule?
Which high priest presided when the council condemned Jesus and tore his robes at the charge of blasphemy?
Which prophetess was consulted by Josiah's officials about the newly found Book of the Law?
Which Moabite woman married Boaz and became the great-grandmother of David?
Which woman of Jericho appears in Joshua 2, in Jesus' genealogy in Matthew 1, and among the examples of faith in Hebrews 11?
Which of the Twelve was absent when Jesus first appeared to the disciples, and later said, 'My Lord and my God'?
Which man named James was executed by Herod Agrippa I?
Which Herod, tetrarch of Galilee, had John the Baptist imprisoned and beheaded?
Which Herod, with Bernice, heard Paul's defense at Caesarea after Festus became governor?
Which governor left Paul imprisoned at Caesarea to please the Jews, when Festus succeeded him?
Which proconsul of Achaia refused to judge the charges brought against Paul at Corinth?
Which coworker of Paul was imprisoned with him at Philippi after Paul cast a spirit out of a slave girl?
Which coworker did Paul leave in Crete to appoint elders in every city?
Which young disciple, son of a Jewish mother and a Greek father, did Paul circumcise before taking him on his journeys?
Which man did Paul send back to Philemon, urging him to receive him as a beloved brother?
Which Ananias was the Damascus disciple sent to restore Saul's sight?
Which prophet's words about a voice crying in the wilderness are applied to John the Baptist in Matthew 3?
Which prophet named Bethlehem as the origin of a ruler, a passage cited to Herod by the chief priests and scribes?
Which prophet's account of a great fish did Jesus cite as a sign of his own burial and resurrection?
Gabriel told Mary her son would receive the throne of which ancestor, to whom an everlasting house was promised through Nathan?
Based on the biblical narrative, which pair could NOT have met during their lifetimes?
Three of these reigned as kings of Judah. Which one did not?
Which sequence lists these kings of Judah in the correct order?
Which sequence lists these kings of Judah in the correct order?
Ruth 4 records that Boaz fathered Obed, Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David. What was Boaz to David?
Who said to Saul that obedience is better than sacrifice, after Saul spared Agag and the best of the flock?
Who said to whom, 'Whither thou goest, I will go'?
Which Persian king, through Esther and Mordecai, issued a decree permitting the Jews to defend themselves on the appointed day?
Which king of Babylon took Jehoiachin into exile and made Zedekiah king in Judah?
Which priest and scribe brought the Book of the Law before the assembly and read it aloud from morning until midday?
AB: Which man went with Barnabas and Saul from Jerusalem to Antioch after their famine-relief visit?
Silas and Judas Barsabbas were sent to Antioch after the Jerusalem Council; Timothy joined Paul later, at Lystra.
Which prophet was told by Amaziah the priest of Bethel to flee to Judah after announcing that Jeroboam would die by the sword?
Hosea and Jonah also belong to Jeroboam II's era, but only Amos was confronted by Amaziah at Bethel; Micah prophesied in Judah.
Which prophet confronted David over Bathsheba and Uriah with the story of a poor man's lamb?
Gad was David's seer and Samuel was already dead; Ahijah belongs to Solomon's later years.
Which son of David tried to make himself king while David lived, with Joab and the priest Abiathar supporting him?
Absalom also rebelled, but earlier, backed by Ahithophel; Adonijah's party included Joab and Abiathar.
Which Pharisee first came to Jesus by night and later brought spices for His burial?
Only Nicodemus is named in both scenes, and he assisted Joseph of Arimathea.
Which Herod had James, the brother of John, killed with the sword and then imprisoned Peter?
Herod the Great ruled at Jesus' birth, Antipas beheaded John the Baptist, and Agrippa II heard Paul at Caesarea.
Which Zechariah was stoned in the court of the LORD's house at the command of King Joash?
Zechariah the father of John the Baptist
The son of Berechiah wrote the prophecy, the son of Jeroboam II was killed by Shallum, and John's father was a priest in Herod's day.
Which man named Judas asked at the Last Supper why Jesus would reveal Himself to the disciples and not to the world?
Iscariot had already left; Barsabbas and the Galilean belong to Acts.
Matthew applies 'Out of Egypt have I called my son' to Jesus' return from Egypt. Which prophet first wrote it, about Israel?
Matthew also cites Micah (2:6) and Jeremiah (2:18) in the same chapter, for different events.
Jesus says who will rise in judgment against that generation because she came from the ends of the earth to hear wisdom?
Jesus names her alongside the men of Nineveh; she visited Solomon.
Which king of Judah, in an account found only in Chronicles, was bound in fetters and taken to Babylon, then restored after humbling himself?
Jehoiakim was bound for Babylon but not restored; Jehoahaz went to Egypt; Zedekiah was blinded.
Which prophet's ministry could NOT have overlapped with the reign of Hezekiah?
Isaiah, Micah and Hosea each name Hezekiah in their opening verses; Jeremiah began in Josiah's thirteenth year.
Matthew 1 makes Salmon the husband of Rahab, then lists Boaz, Obed, Jesse and David in descent. How is Rahab related to David?
Rahab → Boaz → Obed → Jesse → David gives four generations between them.
After the prophets of Baal were slain at the brook Kishon, what did Elijah do next in the narrative?
Told Ahab to eat, since rain was coming
Fled to Beersheba from Jezebel's threat
Jezebel's threat, Horeb and Elisha's call all come later in 1 Kings 19.
Three statements about the priest Jehoiada are correct. Which is NOT?
He was put to death by Joash for rebuking Judah's idolatry
He kept the young Joash hidden in the temple for six years
His wife Jehosheba was a daughter of King Jehoram
He was buried in the City of David among the kings
Joash killed Jehoiada's son Zechariah, not Jehoiada, who died full of years.
Which person fits every clue: belonged to Saul's household; was lame in both feet; was shown kindness by David for Jonathan's sake; had a servant named Ziba?
Mica was his son and Ish-bosheth and Abner were Saul's kin, but only Mephibosheth was lame, was hosted by David, and was served by Ziba.
Which man both hid a hundred prophets from Jezebel and later met Elijah while managing Ahab's household?
The others are Ahab-era prophets who never ran his household.
Which combination of prophet, place and event is correct?
Elisha — Dothan — his servant saw fiery horses and chariots around the hill
Elijah — Dothan — his servant saw fiery horses and chariots around the hill
Elisha — Gilgal — his servant saw fiery horses and chariots around the hill
Elisha — Dothan — Naaman was healed by washing in the Jordan
Each wrong option swaps one element: the prophet, the place, or the event.
Which sequence gives the order of these stops in David's flight from Saul, beginning with his visit to Ahimelech?
David took the showbread at Nob, feigned madness at Gath, gathered men at Adullam, then saved Keilah.
On the first missionary journey, which city did Paul and Barnabas reach between Perga in Pamphylia and Iconium?
Lystra and Derbe come after Iconium; Troas belongs to a later journey.
Jesse fathered David, David fathered Solomon, and Solomon fathered Rehoboam. Which conclusion must follow?
Jesse → David → Solomon → Rehoboam puts Jesse three generations above Rehoboam.
Which statement wrongly gives Elisha an event that belongs to a different prophet?
He called down fire against the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel
He made an iron axe head float at the Jordan
He healed Naaman's leprosy through the Jordan
He multiplied a widow's oil in borrowed vessels
Carmel is Elijah's contest; the other three are recorded of Elisha.
Which speaker and recipient fit the words 'Had Zimri peace, who slew his master?'
Athaliah to Jehoiada in the temple
Jezebel called from her window to Jehu, comparing him to Zimri, who murdered King Elah.
Which two cities did Paul and Silas pass through after leaving Philippi, before reaching Thessalonica?
Neapolis is before Philippi and Berea comes after Thessalonica.
Which book says Satan provoked David to number Israel, where the parallel account says the LORD's anger moved him?
The Chronicles version names Satan; Samuel records the same census with the LORD's anger.
In his speech, which prophet does Stephen quote about Israel carrying the tabernacle of Moloch?
Stephen cites Amos on Israel's idolatry in the wilderness.
Who sent a young prophet to Ramoth-gilead to anoint Jehu king, though Elijah had earlier been told to anoint him?
Elijah received the command, but Elisha carried it out.
Which Simon lodged Peter in his house by the sea at Joppa?
The sorcerer was in Samaria, the Zealot an apostle, and the leper hosted Jesus at Bethany.
Which prophet, active under Jeroboam II, was sent to Nineveh?
Nahum also spoke against Nineveh but is not tied to Jeroboam II; Amos and Hosea preached in Israel.
Which combination of king, prophet and enemy is correct?
Isaiah assured Hezekiah against Sennacherib; each wrong option changes one element.
Which brook, east of the Jordan, did God send Elijah to hide by, where ravens fed him?
Kidron is by Jerusalem, Kishon by Carmel, and Besor near Ziklag.
In which valley did David face Goliath?
Rephaim and Jezreel host other battles; Achor is Achan's valley.
After the Ethiopian's baptism, Philip was found at which city?
Philip then preached northward until he reached Caesarea.
Who was numbered with the eleven after the lot fell between him and Joseph called Barsabas?
Which man served as cupbearer to a Persian king before becoming governor in Judah?
Zerubbabel and Sheshbazzar governed earlier; Ezra was a priest and scribe.
When cleansing the temple, Jesus said 'My house shall be called the house of prayer.' Which prophet wrote those words?
'Den of thieves' is from Jeremiah 7:11, in the same saying.
